relationships.subject: bicuculline
relationships.evidence_quote: bath application of Bicuculline (10 µM) and Strychnine (1 µM) to inhibit gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptors (GABAA) and glycinergic receptors, respectively

relationships.subject: spinal disinhibition
relationships.evidence_quote: spinal disinhibition unmasks neurons responding to Aβ- and Aδ-fibers across all laminae of the DH, with about half coming from a pool of previously silent neurons

relationships.subject: previously silent neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Strikingly, 35% of neurons became WDR neurons, with about 2/3 coming from a pool of previously silent neurons

key_findings: Spinal disinhibition (bicuculline + strychnine) raises responding DH excitatory neurons from ~33% to ~71%, about half from previously silent neurons.
Silent neurons recruited as WDR cells may underlie mechanical allodynia rather than NS-to-WDR conversion.
